=== FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite ===
- scripts/gh_helpers.sh:730-740 | severity=BLOCKER | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The mutation detector strips text after every `#` without accounting for quoted GraphQL strings, allowing a quoted `#` to hide subsequent `mutation` operations.
  WHY: A GraphQL query containing `"#"` (e.g., `query { f(arg: "#") } mutation { ... }`) results in `mutation` being stripped, causing it to be incorrectly classified as a read (retryable) operation. If the query fails transiently *after the mutation part has been applied by the server*, the retry helper will re-send the mutation, leading to duplicate execution.
- scripts/gh_api_retry.py:117-127 | severity=BLOCKER | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The Python mutation detector shares the same flaw as the bash version, failing to account for quoted `#` characters.
  WHY: Same as above; Python-based callers (e.g., orchestrator label readers, audit scripts) will incorrectly retry non-idempotent GraphQL mutations.
=== END FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite ===

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- scripts/gh_helpers.sh line 730-740 (bash `${_line%%#*}`); scripts/gh_api_retry.py line 117-127 (Python `line.split("#", 1)[0]`) | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: Both implementations strip everything after the first `#` on every line as if it were a GraphQL comment, so a `#` inside a string literal can hide a subsequent mutation operation.
  WHY: A GraphQL document containing `#` inside a string on the same line as a later mutation operation is misclassified as a read; if `gh api` returns a transient 5xx after GitHub has applied the mutation, the helper retries and applies it a second time.
